## 0aead82893c5

**Reproduced teaching shortcut; target left unchanged.** The canonical-fitting rival is: when more than one object has the same mask-symmetry class, keep the **first** object in row-major scan order instead of the authority’s last-object overwrite, then pack the same four classes into the same 2×2 gallery.

The rival matches all three canonical training outputs because each canonical has exactly one object per class. It also survives complete generated lessons whenever no duplicate-class example appears. Using 500 independent four-demo windows per difficulty (`seed = window_index`, sample indexes 0–3), it survived all four demonstrations in 155/500 windows for easy, 155/500 for medium, and 155/500 for hard. The exact easy surviving window is seed 6; all four generated inputs pass `self_check`, and supported Racket application confirms the rival output equals the authority output for each.

The rival is not vacuous: on valid generated input `difficulty="easy", seed=0, sample_index=2`, input SHA-256 `f62db78bc96ec82ad587efbb16c245ec73c5e4554f21186e4ff553034fc25529`, two `both`-symmetric objects differ. The authority output SHA-256 is `6c4dc6bf1778e3a411f5ac206302ee19e8647316f95966492c8e23a3be747074`; the first-wins rival output SHA-256 is `f92e9d898fa4ba0b5a18cd6712fbd27e38e2262009b5027c71c8cb02a7300da9`.

Evidence: `checks/audit/0aead82893c5/first-wins-audit.json`, with exact inputs, outputs, canonical checks, generator/rule hashes, sampler, and domain caveat; `checks/audit/0aead82893c5/racket.json` is the authority receipt. The empirical window policy is explicit and is not claimed to cover every possible lesson assembler.

## 0aead82893c5

**Reproduced teaching shortcut; target left unchanged.** A plausible rival keeps the **first** object encountered in row-major scan order when two objects share a mask-symmetry class, instead of the authority's last-object overwrite, then packs the four classes into the same 2×2 gallery.

The rival fits all 4/4 canonical pairs because each canonical input has one object per class. In an independent census of 100 four-demo windows per difficulty (`seed=0..99`, sample indexes `0..3`), it survived all demonstrations in 24/100 easy, 24/100 medium, and 24/100 hard windows. This bulk census uses the generator's Python rule mirror; the exact disagreement below is separately checked by the selected Racket authority.

Exact valid counterexample: `difficulty="easy", seed=0, sample_index=2, texture="duplicate_class"`, generator SHA-256 `9a70fb5b08f3e1b384a80b4b199f6d886dd5ab5657e4356bebaa30e0ed4e69d1`, input SHA-256 `f62db78bc96ec82ad587efbb16c245ec73c5e4554f21186e4ff553034fc25529`. `self_check` returns no reasons. The public Racket apply receipt gives authority output SHA-256 `6c4dc6bf1778e3a411f5ac206302ee19e8647316f95966492c8e23a3be747074`; first-wins gives `f92e9d898fa4ba0b5a18cd6712fbd27e38e2262009b5027c71c8cb02a7300da9`.

Evidence: `checks/audit/0aead82893c5/first-wins-audit.json`, `input.json`, `racket.json`, and `rival.json`. Domain caveat: the sampled-window rate is finite evidence for the stated assembler, not an exhaustive rate for every lesson construction.

## 0aead82893c5

**Classification: reproduced generated-domain validator/oracle mismatch.**

I checked selected generator SHA-256
`9a70fb5b08f3e1b384a80b4b199f6d886dd5ab5657e4356bebaa30e0ed4e69d1`
and rule hash `8b1372f0ce7c`. I specifically tested whether nested/overlapping bounding boxes
make the generator’s component-only symmetry validation disagree with the
selected rule’s whole-crop symmetry classification.

The generator itself produced the witness at seed 591, sample index 2,
difficulty `hard`, override `{"texture": "duplicate_class"}`. It passes
`self_check` with no problems. For the color-8 component at bounding box
`[9, 9, 14, 14]`:

- the component’s own cells are symmetric both horizontally and vertically;
- the entire bounding-box crop contains three nonzero cells belonging to another
  object and is symmetric in neither direction.

The selected Racket rule uses the whole crop, whereas the component-only rival
uses the pure mask. Their outputs differ in **32 cells**. Thus this is a lawful
generated input under the target’s own validator whose semantic class differs
from what that validator checks; it can teach accidental cross-object
interactions rather than the stated per-component property.

Exact generator parameters, component cells/classes, differing-cell preview,
source hashes, and command are in `checks/audit/0aead82893c5/repro.json`.
`input.json`, actual `racket.json`, and `rival.json` retain the complete grids.

The audit target was left unchanged as required.

## 0aead82893c5

Evidence directory: `checks/audit/0aead82893c5/`; bare filenames in this section are relative to that directory.

**Concrete findings: reproduced generated-domain semantic mismatch; advertised override-range defect. Audited source unchanged.**

The existing unresolved crop-contamination finding remains reproducible on the assigned generator. Regenerating `seed=591`, `sample_index=2`, `difficulty="hard"`, overrides `{"texture":"duplicate_class"}` produces a 15×18 board with `self_check == []`. The color-8 component is a 6×6 hollow square at zero-based bounding box `[9,9,14,14]`: its own mask has both symmetries, but its bounding box contains three color-4 cells. The selected Racket rule classifies that whole crop as neither. Later scan-order overwrite leaves the color-2 object in the top-left gallery cell. The component-only rival instead puts the color-8 square there. Actual Racket and rival outputs differ in **32 cells**. This independently regenerates and executes the retained `review-ddc5d378b2baefde:v0001` witness; it is not claimed as a newly discovered semantic issue.

The complete input is `checks/audit/0aead82893c5/input.json`; the actual public Racket output and receipt are `checks/audit/0aead82893c5/racket.json`; the diagnostic rival is `checks/audit/0aead82893c5/rival.json`. Racket reports `valid_output=true`, no error, and the rule hash matches the catalog. The input SHA-256 is `31cf0e12ec82cb7650e2dc2a87afafab7139d9d24b607de192f6724fa149ae32`; the Racket output SHA-256 is `895bcda4ba35991855351c860599d34ea50d038a90e525e4c60d8f2e30b309b6`.

A separate override check finds a concrete contract mismatch. `AXES` advertises `grid_h=10..18` and `grid_w=12..22`; with `seed=0`, `sample_index=0`, and no difficulty, each single-field endpoint override is rejected before producing a grid:

| Override | Actual exception |
|---|---|
| `grid_h=10` | `ValueError: draw_int('grid_h'): override 10 outside [11, 15]` |
| `grid_h=18` | `ValueError: draw_int('grid_h'): override 18 outside [11, 15]` |
| `grid_w=12` | `ValueError: draw_int('grid_w'): override 12 outside [14, 18]` |
| `grid_w=22` | `ValueError: draw_int('grid_w'): override 22 outside [14, 18]` |

For these four rejected calls, an input, self-check result, and Racket output do not exist. Their arguments and exceptions are retained in `construction.json` and `audit_result.json`.

**Bound and controls.** Two public `apply` calls executed eight total inputs: the witness, all three canonical training pairs and the canonical test pair, plus one generated control for each helpful texture (`seed=23`, hard, indexes 0/1/2, respectively plain/same_color/duplicate_class). All eight Racket outputs are valid. The four canonical labels match their stored outputs, and the component-only rival matches all four canonical pairs. The three generated controls pass self-check. This is a bounded reproduction and four override probes, not an exhaustive search or a rate estimate. Python outputs are diagnostics/rivals only; actual labels come from Racket.

**Exact source binding.** Generator SHA-256: `9a70fb5b08f3e1b384a80b4b199f6d886dd5ab5657e4356bebaa30e0ed4e69d1`. Executed rule hash: `8b1372f0ce7c`. Executed rule-text SHA-256: `f463e91b82caf0c519beaf4e72117a6fe110587eed8348a482c483dffe0db93d`. Both public command exit codes are 0. Exact argv, outer/effective cwd, stdout/stderr paths and receipts are in `checks/audit/0aead82893c5/apply_commands.json`; full comparisons and command records are in `audit_result.json`. No audited generator or rule bytes were edited.
